desc:
A company has n employees numbered 0..n-1. The array manager gives each employee's direct manager, and the head of the company has manager[head] = -1. The company hierarchy is a tree rooted at the head.

The head learns some news at time 0. An employee who learns it needs informTime[e] minutes to tell all of their direct subordinates at once (they all hear it exactly informTime[e] minutes later). Employees without subordinates have informTime = 0. Return the number of minutes until every employee knows the news.

manager    = [-1, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2]
informTime = [ 3, 2, 4, 0, 0, 0]

employees 1 and 2 hear at 3, employees 3 and 4 at 3+2 = 5, employee 5 at 3+4 = 7   -> 7
constraints: Exactly one employee has manager -1; every other manager[e] is a valid employee number and the hierarchy is a tree
0 ≤ informTime[e] ≤ 1,000 (informTime[e] is 0 when e has no subordinates)
hints: When does an employee hear the news? Think of the chain of managers above them.
An employee hears it at the sum of informTime of all their managers on the way up to the head. The answer is the largest such sum over all employees.

Build the list of subordinates of each manager and traverse from the head, passing down the time at which each employee hears the news (parent's time plus the parent's informTime). Use a stack or queue instead of recursion.
editorial: Model the hierarchy as a rooted tree. If employee e hears at time t[e], then each direct subordinate s hears at t[e] + informTime[e], because the manager tells everybody in one go. So t[head] = 0 and the answer is the maximum of t over all employees (which is always attained at a leaf).

Build subordinates lists from the manager array, then traverse top-down with a stack, storing the arrival time of each employee. This is O(n) time and space. A recursive DFS gives the same result but the hierarchy can be 100,000 levels deep (a chain), so prefer an iterative traversal.

Notice that the time spent by a manager does not depend on how many subordinates there are, only on the manager. This is why the answer is simply the heaviest root-to-leaf path when each node is weighted by its informTime.
